title: One of the seventeen records obs-2026-08-19-1.json found echoing the notary's own fetch time has stopped: gdacs-fl-1103815's datemodified froze on 2026-09-03 and has stayed frozen across two more observed nights, ending a 26-night unbroken echo run right when the underlying source itself stopped touching the record
statement: obs-2026-08-19-1.json named 17 OPEN GDACS futures whose properties.datemodified advanced to match the notary's own fetch time on every observed night despite zero REVISED events in foreknown/registry.json, and left open (in the review note it added to sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json) whether that 17-record set was stable membership or would drift over more nights, and whether datemodified could ever be shown to discriminate genuine source activity from feed-generation echo for this class of record at all. Checked against every snapshot from 2026-08-08 (the observatory's first night) through 2026-09-07, gdacs-fl-1103815 -- one of the original 17, a China flood (glide FL-2026-000148-CHN, still status OPEN, still a single NOTARIZED history event, its own fromdate/todate window 2026-03-25 to 2026-04-14 already almost five months closed) -- had a datemodified that matched that night's own calendar date on all 26 consecutive observed nights from 2026-08-08 through 2026-09-03 without a single exception, tracking the notary's fetch time exactly as the echo pattern predicts. Starting with the first snapshot taken after the 2026-09-04/2026-09-05 notary gap (obs-2026-09-06-1.json), its datemodified stopped advancing: 2026-09-06's snapshot and 2026-09-07's snapshot both read the identical value 2026-09-03T13:36:40 -- a genuine, source-issued timestamp several hours later than that day's own snapshot capture (2026-09-03T09:09:19), not a generic placeholder or a repeat of a prior night's value. No other field for this record (alertlevel, episodealertlevel, severitydata, fromdate, todate) changed across this or any surrounding night. Of the other 16 records from the original 17, every one is still echoing the fetch time on 2026-09-07 with zero exceptions; two further records not present in the original 17 (gdacs-eq-1558059, announced 2026-08-15; gdacs-wf-1030534, announced 2026-08-21) have since joined the same echoing set. gdacs-fl-1103815 is the only record, in this observatory's entire history, that has ever left the echoing set while remaining OPEN and unrevised -- every other member either joined it or has stayed in it.
method: For each date directory under foreknown/snapshots/ (26 available, 2026-08-08 through 2026-09-07, honouring the observatory's own gaps at 2026-08-10/11 and 2026-09-04/05), loaded gdacs.json and extracted the single feature with eventtype=='FL', eventid==1103815, printing properties.datemodified and properties.iscurrent for each night to confirm the unbroken 26-night same-date match followed by the two-night freeze. Separately, for 2026-09-01/02/03 (three consecutive nights before the gap) and 2026-09-06/07 (the two consecutive nights after), computed the full set of OPEN GDACS futures whose properties.iscurrent=='false', properties.datemodified starts with that night's own date, and whose foreknown/registry.json history contains no REVISED or CORRECTED event (the same construction obs-2026-08-19-1.json used, generalised past its original 3-night window). Intersected the pre-gap and post-gap sets against each other and against the original 17 ids obs-2026-08-19-1.json named, to isolate exactly which ids persisted, which (if any) dropped, and which joined.
worth_watching_because: sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json has stayed PROPOSED since 2026-08-13 partly because its falsification clause names a real risk it never had a counter-example for: that datemodified might not be a per-record 'source re-examined this' signal at all for long-idle records, only an artefact of GDACS's feed generation that would read every dormant record as maximally fresh forever. Tonight's finding is the first case in this observatory's history where that fear is directly testable and comes out the other way for at least one record: gdacs-fl-1103815 broke a 26-night unbroken lockstep with the fetch time at the exact moment (2026-09-03T13:36:40, several hours past that day's own capture) the source's own timestamp says it was last touched, and has stayed broken for two more nights while the other 16 original members and 2 later arrivals kept advancing normally. A days_since_datemodified_changed counter, had it been running, would have correctly started counting for this one record on 2026-09-03 while reading zero for everyone else in the set -- exactly the discrimination the sensor's test_rule needs and the falsification clause worried might not exist. This does not settle promotion: the ~18-member echoing set's own behaviour (advancing every night with no underlying activity) is unaddressed by a single counter-example, and the proposal's 2026-08-17/2026-08-19 reviews already named that as the open design question. A review note citing this observation is added to sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json rather than promoting it tonight.
left_alone: Not promoting sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json: one record breaking from the echo pattern demonstrates the signal can discriminate, but the test_rule as written would still report all 18 remaining echo-set members as freshly touched indefinitely, which is the unresolved design question the 2026-08-17/2026-08-19 reviews already identified and this observation does not redesign. Not reviewing sensor-lead-time-pathway-idle.json tonight beyond confirming its count: foreknown/resolutions/ holds 8 FORECAST-kind resolutions (all NO_ALERT_MATCH, checked against foreknown/registry.json's 11 total FORECAST futures), still short of the N=10 threshold the proposal's own test_rule names, so no new data point exists to record. Not adding a foreknown-notary-hole-accounting entry for the 2026-09-04/2026-09-05 gap: that step's one precedent (autonomy/log.jsonl, 2026-08-28T09:43:35+00:00) was written by a separate scheduled keeper routine under a distinct standing delegation, not by a discovery pass, and discovery/PROMPT.md does not name hole-accounting among what this pass may produce. Not writing a memory-hole verdicts file: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-06.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 82 entries. Not touching sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json: gdacs-tc-1001305 (its only live case) is still OPEN and has not closed a second time since its 2026-09-03 revision.
